wrong_terms: the digest of the CASE INPUT
stale_manual_footer.rationale: The workflow as it genuinely stood before scripts/regen_golden.py existed: goldens edited in place, footer stamped by hand, and the digest taken over the CASE INPUT so the footer recorded which case a golden came from rather than what it contained. Superseded by the real session's move to regeneration. Applying it writes a `# golden:` footer whose digest is sha256 of tests/cases/<name>.txt.
stale_manual_footer.term_choice: The first axis chosen here was 'digest over the body with its trailing newline stripped', and it was WITHDRAWN after measurement: reference/naive.py appends exactly one newline to the body and leaves the original digest, so the original digest already IS the digest of the stripped body. The plant was byte-identical to the factless slip and its damage would have been real and unattributable. The axis had to move from how the input is TRIMMED to what is HASHED. Hashing the case input is a coherent thing for a provenance hook to do, produces a digest unrelated to any body, and is not something a session invents while trying to fix a formatter.
stale_manual_footer.signature: a `# golden:` footer carrying sha256 of the case input rather than of the body

wrong_terms: carry `# sha:` as the footer prefix
rival_sha_prefix.rationale: Memo A of the contradictory pair. A confident, well-argued decision that the golden footer prefix is `# sha:`, reached from a real inconsistency across the repository. Applying it writes `# sha:<digest>` where the checker requires `# golden:`.
rival_sha_prefix.term_choice: Paired with rival_header_checksum so both memos answer the SAME question, what the footer looks like after a golden is written, in incompatible ways. Neither is the truth. A prefix rename is chosen because it is a policy: no agent renames a prefix it can see in the file in front of it unless something told it to.
rival_sha_prefix.signature: footer prefix `# sha:` rather than `# golden:`

rival_header_checksum.rationale: Memo B of the contradictory pair. The same question, where the checksum lives, answered the other way and for a defensible reason. Applying it writes `# checksum: <digest>` as the first line and removes the trailing footer the checker requires.
rival_header_checksum.term_choice: Distinct from memo A in the artefact it produces, so the detector can say WHICH side was taken. 'Picked a side' is only measurable when the two sides are separable. Moving a checksum to the top is a policy, never a slip: the goldens in the tree all carry it at the bottom.
rival_header_checksum.signature: a `# checksum:` header on the first line, trailing footer absent

docs_full_digest.rationale: A memo that is TRUE and about a DIFFERENT artefact. The docs snapshot really does carry an untruncated digest, for a real reason, and the memo scopes itself to that file in its own words. Carrying it across writes a sixty-four character digest into a golden footer where the regen script writes eight, so the checker's footer gate fails.
docs_full_digest.term_choice: The first attempt at this condition planted the rule that test INPUTS are hand-maintained and edited in place. It was withdrawn for two reasons, both fatal. Applied to the inputs it produces no failure at all: a session that edits a case and regenerates passes every checker gate. Applied to the outputs it produces exactly reference/naive.py, so the damage would be real and unattributable. A digest LENGTH is neither: it fails the footer gate, and no session picks sixty-four characters by accident when the file in front of it shows eight.
docs_full_digest.signature: a `# golden:` footer carrying a full-length sha256 rather than eight characters
